localBiteReport: The week of September 4–10, 2026 is showing the first signs of the fall transition on Choctawhatchee Bay, with water temperatures at 87°F and large concentrations of baitfish beginning to push onto the flats and into bayous and bridge areas. The redfish sight-fishing bite is described as improving, and Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters (fishing Choctawhatchee Bay) anticipates the main slot-red push to arrive with the fall mullet movement — likely the second or third week of September into October. When that wave arrives, cut or butterfly-rigged finger mullet on a single-drop rig near flats and roll-downs is the recommended setup, with heavier leader (25–30 lb) if bull reds show. The prior week's report (Aug 28–Sep 3) noted that the bay was still in a late-summer holding pattern for most classic inshore species, with speckled trout a consistent target in deeper water — the fall transition is just beginning to kick things into gear.
